# arianet_floating_ip (Resource)

A floating IP. Maps to `/cloud/v1/floating-ips` and its `assign`/`unassign`/`change_dns_ptr` actions.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "arianet_floating_ip" "public" {
  datacenter = "eu-central-1"
  type       = "ipv4"
  name       = "public"
  dns_ptr    = "www.example.com"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `datacenter` (String) Datacenter code. Changing it replaces the IP.
- `type` (String) `ipv4` or `ipv6`. Changing it replaces the IP.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Description.
- `dns_ptr` (String) Reverse DNS (PTR) hostname of the IP.
- `labels` (Map of String) User-defined labels (key/value pairs). Lists can be filtered by them with a label selector.
- `name` (String) Name.
- `project_id` (Number) ID of the project the resource is in. Defaults to the account's default project; changing it moves the resource.
- `protection_delete` (Boolean) Whether the resource is protected from deletion. Must be set to false before the resource can be destroyed.
- `server_id` (Number) Server the IP is assigned to. Do not combine with `arianet_floating_ip_assignment`.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) Creation time (RFC 3339).
- `id` (String) Floating IP ID.
- `ip_address` (String) The IP address.
- `status` (String) Status.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import arianet_floating_ip.public 9
```
